questions.question: After you connect the air lines to the trailer, what should you do next?
questions.correctAnswerText: Send air to the trailer.
questions.explanation: Coupling and uncoupling trailers safely is critical when driving a combination vehicle. After connecting the air lines to the trailer, send air to the trailer.

questions.question: Keeping cargo centered on a truck helps to:
questions.correctAnswerText: Stop a rollover.
questions.explanation: A truck is more likely to roll over if the cargo is loaded unevenly. Keep the load centered on the truck to help prevent a dangerous rollover.

questions.question: Which of these will NOT help prevent a truck from rolling over?

options.text: Keeping cargo as low to the ground as possible
Driving on the shoulder of a road

questions.correctAnswerText: Driving on the shoulder of a road
questions.explanation: To prevent a truck rollover, keep cargo weight as low as possible when loading. Drive slowly around turns. Driving on the road shoulder will not help prevent a rollover.

questions.question: How do you test the tractor protection valve?

options.text: Release air by pressing the brake pedal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release air by pressing the brake pedal.
questions.explanation: To test the tractor protection valve, let the air supply charge fully. Turn off the engine. Then press the brake pedal several times to release air. The valve should move to emergency position when air pressure drops too low.

questions.question: How much space should there be between the upper and lower fifth wheel?
questions.correctAnswerText: No space
questions.explanation: Before each trip, check all couplings. There should be no space between the upper and lower fifth wheel.

questions.question: What happens if a trailer is too high?
questions.correctAnswerText: It may not couple correctly.
questions.explanation: Before coupling a tractor and trailer, check the trailer height. A low trailer can damage the nose. A high trailer may not couple correctly.

questions.question: What is the best way to tell your trailer is skidding?

options.text: Watch the trailer in your mirrors.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watch the trailer in your mirrors.
questions.explanation: The easiest way to notice your trailer is skidding is to watch it in your mirrors. This also lets you catch skidding early.

questions.question: During a trip, which valves should be open?

options.text: The rear service line shut-off valve
The rear supply line shut-off valve

questions.correctAnswerText: The inner shut-off valves
questions.explanation: When starting a trip, open all shut-off valves except the last ones at the rear of the trailer. Air must reach the brakes on all trailers and not escape from the back of the vehicle.

questions.question: During a trip, landing gear should be:
questions.correctAnswerText: Completely raised.
questions.explanation: Landing gear must always be completely raised before driving. If landing gear is not fully raised, it can catch on railroad tracks or other road hazards.

questions.question: When pulling a trailer, where should the air supply control lever be?
questions.correctAnswerText: Normal
questions.explanation: Older vehicles use levers instead of knobs for tractor protection controls. Set the air supply control to "normal" position to properly pull a trailer.

questions.question: Fully-loaded rigs:

options.text: Are more likely to roll over than empty rigs.

questions.correctAnswerText: Are more likely to roll over than empty rigs.
questions.explanation: Fully-loaded rigs are more likely to roll over than empty rigs. The heavy cargo raises the center of gravity, making rollovers more dangerous.

questions.question: Combination vehicles:

options.text: Are usually shorter than single commercial vehicles.
Usually need less skill to drive than single commercial vehicles.
Usually need more skill to drive than single commercial vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Usually need more skill to drive than single commercial vehicles.
questions.explanation: Combination vehicles need more skill to drive than single commercial vehicles. They are longer, heavier, and roll over more easily.

questions.question: If you are backing and are unsure of your path, you should:

options.text: Stop and get out to check.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and get out to check.
questions.explanation: If you are unsure about backing, stop the vehicle and get out to check your path before continuing.

questions.question: More than half of all truck driver deaths from accidents are caused by:
questions.correctAnswerText: Rollovers.
questions.explanation: Rollovers cause more than half of truck driver deaths from accidents. To prevent rollovers, load cargo low and centered on your rig, and take corners slowly.

questions.question: Watching the road ahead:

options.text: Is more dangerous than only watching mirrors.
Does not help you drive safer.
Can help you avoid sudden lane changes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can help you avoid sudden lane changes.
questions.explanation: Watching ahead helps you see obstacles early. This way, you can avoid making dangerous sudden lane changes while driving a combination vehicle.

questions.question: Before a trip, you can check that air reaches all trailers by:

options.text: Checking for moving air inside each trailer.
Listening for air at the rear shut-off valve.
Feeling for air at the front shut-off valve.

questions.correctAnswerText: Listening for air at the rear shut-off valve.
questions.explanation: Before a trip, make sure air reaches all trailers. Open the shut-off valves on the rear of the last trailer and listen for air. If air escapes, the air system is working for the entire vehicle.

questions.question: Combination vehicles:

options.text: Often have taller trailers than single commercial vehicles.
Are usually lighter than single commercial vehicles.
Need more skill to drive than single commercial vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Need more skill to drive than single commercial vehicles.
questions.explanation: Combination vehicles need more skill to drive than single commercial vehicles. They are longer, heavier, and roll over more easily.

questions.question: When coupling:

options.text: You can assume all vehicles are the same.
Cracks in the mounting are acceptable.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure you couple correctly.
questions.explanation: Incorrect coupling and uncoupling of combination vehicles can be extremely dangerous.

questions.question: Bobtail tractors are ____ to stop than tractors attached to full semitrailers.
questions.correctAnswerText: More difficult
questions.explanation: A bobtail is a tractor with no semitrailer attached. Bobtails are harder to stop and need more distance to stop than a loaded tractor with a semitrailer.

questions.question: When coupling a trailer:

options.text: Make sure to connect the matching glad hands.
Glad hands can be connected to any glad hands.
Only one set of glad hands should be connected.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure to connect the matching glad hands.
questions.explanation: When coupling, connect matching glad hands. They are often color-coded to help you avoid mistakes. Blue is usually for service lines and red is usually for emergency lines.
